passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion and analysis provides information that management believes is relevant to an assessment and understanding of Qnity’s financial condition and results of operations. Management’s discussion and analysis of financial condition and results of operations is provided as a supplement to, and should be read in conjunction with, the Consolidated Financial Statements and related notes to enhance the understanding of the Company’s operations and present business environment. This discussion and analysis contains forward-looking statements and involves numerous risks and uncertainties, including, but not limited to, those discussed in this “Management’s Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations” and “Risk Factors” in this Annual Report. Carefully read the information under “Cautionary Note Regarding Forward-Looking Statements” in this Annual Report. Qnity assumes no obligation to update any of these forward-looking statements except as required by law. Actual results may differ materially from those contained in any forward-looking statements. BUSINESS OVERVIEW We are one of the largest global leaders in materials and solutions for the semiconductor and electronics industries. We empower our customers’ technology roadmaps to enable advancements in megatrends such as AI, high-performance computing and advanced connectivity. We partner with leading semiconductor and advanced device manufacturers to address complex challenges and develop solutions that facilitate next-generation technological innovations. With over 50 years of experience in systems engineering and material science, a global manufacturing footprint, and major application labs across the world, we are well-positioned to capitalize on emerging opportunities across various sectors including data centers, communications infrastructure, industrials, automotive, and consumer electronics. We are organized into two operating segments: • Semiconductor Technologies: Our Semiconductor Technologies segment provides a portfolio of innovative materials and solutions utilized across multiple stages of the semiconductor manufacturing process. These advanced materials are qualified into customers’ roadmaps, designed to improve chip performance, enhance yield and enable leading-edge node technology. • Interconnect Solutions: Our Interconnect Solutions segment offers what we believe to be a comprehensive range of best-in-class material solutions that address the evolving complexities of signal integrity, thermal and power management and advanced packaging. These solutions are integral for advanced electronics hardware, including complex printed circuit boards and advanced semiconductor packaging. Our broad portfolio of solutions and materials across both Semiconductor Technologies and Interconnect Solutions segments positions us as a comprehensive solutions provider for our customers. We are often the partner of choice due to our strong innovation capabilities and extensive materials and engineering expertise. passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: You should carefully consider the following risks and other information in this Annual Report on Form 10-K in evaluating us and our common stock. Any of the following risks, as well as additional risks and uncertainties not currently known to us, beyond our control or that we currently deem immaterial, could materially and adversely affect our business, results of operations or financial condition. Based on current information, we believe that the following identifies the most significant risks that could affect our business, results of operations or financial condition. Risks Related to Our Business Our results are affected by competitive conditions and customer preferences. We operate in a highly competitive, global industry. Some of our competitors may have better-established customer relationships than we do, which may enable them to have their products specified for use more frequently and more quickly by these customers. Further, customers continually evaluate the benefits of internal manufacturing versus outsourcing, and a customer’s decision to internally manufacture products that we provide may negatively impact us. If we are unable to maintain our competitive position, we could experience downward pressure on prices, fewer customer orders, reduced margins, the inability to take advantage of new business opportunities and a loss of market share, any of which could have a material adverse effect on our results of operations. Further, we expect that existing and new competitors will improve their products and introduce new products with enhanced performance characteristics. The introduction of new products, more efficient production of existing products, or products sold at a lower cost by competitors could diminish our market share and increase pricing pressure on our products. Our competitors include companies outside of the U.S., including companies in countries where foreign governments seek to build a domestic-centric semiconductor ecosystem. From time to time, governments around the world may provide incentives or make other investments that could benefit and give competitive advantages to our competitors. Government incentives may not be available to us on acceptable terms or at all. If our competitors can benefit from such government incentives and we cannot, it could strengthen our competitors’ relative position and have a material adverse effect on our business. We expect the demand for product offerings that align with sustainability goals (in areas such as substances of concern, circular economy, waste, water, nature/biodiversity, responsible procurement, human rights) to continue to increase, driven by end-user and customer demand, investor preference and government legislative and market-responsive product-specific actions. Failure to timely react to these trends and manage our product portfolio and innovation activities responsively could decrease the competitiveness of our products and result in the de-selection of us as a partner of choice. credit_strengths.text: Operating margin sits above the sector median, reflecting qualified, roadmap-embedded materials positions in Semiconductor Technologies and Interconnect Solutions that support pricing and mix. Profitability of this order underpins cash generation through the cycle, though the margin comparison is a single-period snapshot and prior-year direction is unavailable.

Interest coverage is comfortably above the sector median and far above unity, with operating income dwarfing gross interest expense. The debt stack is largely long-dated, with only a small current maturity, so refinancing pressure in the near term is limited and the coupon burden is modest relative to earnings.

key_risks.text: Gross and net leverage both sit above the sector median, placing the issuer in the intermediate indicative risk band rather than the stronger cohort. Headroom to the next leverage boundary is moderate, so a meaningful EBITDA decline or incremental debt-funded action would compress the cushion quickly.

The risk factors flag intense global competition, customer in-sourcing of production, and government incentives benefiting rivals building domestic semiconductor ecosystems. Pricing pressure or loss of design wins would erode the qualified-position moat and could reduce margins and volumes, weakening the cash flow that services the debt stack.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Operating cash flow covers capital expenditure and dividends by a wide margin, and free cash flow covers dividends many times over, leaving substantial discretionary cash after maintenance investment. Buyback data is unavailable, so total shareholder distributions cannot be assessed and the residual cushion for debt reduction remains uncertain.

Cash flow to debt and free cash flow to debt both trail the sector median, indicating the balance sheet carries more debt per unit of cash generation than peers. Liquidity is adequate, with a current ratio above the sector median and a cash buffer, but the debt stock is concentrated in a single long-dated bullet.

overall_credit_view.text: The indicative financial risk profile is intermediate, driven by leverage above the sector median offset by strong coverage and solid free cash flow conversion. Our judgement is that the credit is investment-grade in character but sits in the weaker half of the technology cohort on balance-sheet metrics, with limited cushion to absorb a cyclical downturn.

The maturity ladder is benign, with only a small amortization in each of the coming years and the bulk of principal due beyond the visible horizon, so refinancing risk is low near term. We would monitor competitive pressure on margins and any debt-funded distributions that push leverage toward the next risk boundary.

credit_strengths.text: 營業利潤率處於行業中位數之上，反映半導體技術及互連解決方案中具備資格、嵌入路線圖的材料定位，支撐定價及產品組合。此等盈利水平支撐整個週期的現金產生，惟利潤率比較屬單一期間的快照，且缺乏上一年度的方向性數據。
利息覆蓋率穩居行業中位數之上，且遠高於一，經營收入遠超總利息支出。債務結構大部分為長年期，僅有少量即期到期，故短期再融資壓力有限，票息負擔相對盈利而言適中。

key_risks.text: 總槓桿及淨槓桿均高於行業中位數，令發行人處於中間指示性風險區間，而非較強組別。距下一槓桿界限的緩衝屬中等，故EBITDA顯著下降或增量債務融資行動將迅速壓縮緩衝。
風險因素指出全球競爭激烈、客戶將生產內包，以及政府激勵措施惠及建立本土半導體生態系統的競爭對手。定價壓力或失去設計訂單將侵蝕具資格定位的護城河，並可能降低利潤率及銷量，削弱償付債務結構的現金流。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 經營現金流大幅覆蓋資本開支及股息，自由現金流覆蓋股息多倍，於維持性投資後留下大量可自由支配現金。回購數據不可得，故無法評估股東分派總額，用於減債的剩餘緩衝仍不確定。
現金流對債務比率及自由現金流對債務比率均落後於行業中位數，顯示資產負債表每單位現金產生所承載的債務多於同業。流動性充足，流動比率高於行業中位數並有現金緩衝，惟債務存量集中於單一長年期子彈式到期。

overall_credit_view.text: 指示性財務風險狀況為中等，驅動因素為槓桿高於行業中位數，並由強勁覆蓋率及穩健的自由現金流轉換所抵銷。我們的判斷是，該信貸在性質上屬投資級，惟按資產負債表指標計處於科技組別中較弱的一半，吸收週期性下行的緩衝有限。
到期階梯良性，未來各年僅有少量攤還，本金大部分於可見期限之後到期，故短期再融資風險低。我們將監測利潤率所受的競爭壓力，以及任何將槓桿推向下一風險界限的債務融資分派。
